text: With the pipeline planned, Marcus plans where its images run: dev, staging, and prod namespaces inside one EKS cluster, not three separate clusters.
Catalog-api is read-heavy and steady -- it gets a tight, predictable resource plan. Checkout-api spikes hard around on-sales, so it's planned with autoscaling headroom instead.
Rollout is planned as a rolling update: new pods must pass a readiness probe before traffic shifts, and old pods only terminate once the new ones are ready.
Promotion is staged -- dev, then staging, then prod -- so nothing reaches production without clearing the environments before it.
Next: planning how the team will actually know this is healthy once real traffic hits it.
